page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor and the x86_64 CPU architecture. The system features 20 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation model, paired with 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. Acceleration is provided by three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined total of 72 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning external block storage must be provisioned separately for operating system and data storage needs. Network connectivity includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A key architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention under sustained, non-GPU compute-heavy workloads, though the primary processing power is oriented toward the dedicated GPU hardware.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high GPU resource density by bundling three enterprise-grade accelerators with a substantial memory footprint, making it a viable option for workloads that require high VRAM capacity without the overhead of dedicated, non-shared CPU cores. Appropriate workloads include GPU-accelerated machine learning inference, data science tasks, video transcoding, and parallel processing jobs that leverage CUDA or the Ada Lovelace architecture.
